newsitem.title: BURMA: Suu Kyi says Burma still holding people after student unrest.
newsitem.headline: Suu Kyi says Burma still holding people after student unrest.

text.p: Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi said on Monday that the ruling military government still held 105 detainees after December anti-government street protests.
She said as far as she knew, 24 of them were students, 34 were members and supporters of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party, 18 were NLD youths and 29 were non-NLD members.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) had said on Saturday that there were no more detainees being held in connection with the student unrest.
The Nobel laureate also condemned closed trial of detainees by the government and the lack of provision of counsel to those defendants.
The government recently announced that 34 people, including some NLD members had been jailed in connection with the student unrest without mentioning trial.

Suu Kyi also said that she did not need the government to look after her personal security so that she could be able to move around more freely. The SLORC has said that public access to Suu Kyi was blocked because it wanted to ensure her personal security and such barriers would be removed only after the situation improved.
